statement: NVIDIA's official marketplace lists the RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell at $13,250 in August 2026, a 55% increase in roughly 16 months from its March 2025 launch MSRP of $8,565.
why: This is a hardware price level with a stated baseline and a quantified change, so it functions as a confirmation overlay on how tight professional-class GPU hardware supply is.

impact.mechanism: A large official-list price rise on a high-memory professional card points to constrained memory and card supply feeding through to buyer cost; as a price row it is a display overlay only.

evidence.excerpt: NVIDIA's official marketplace lists the card at $13,250

confidence.basis: A cloud-GPU vendor's own blog, an interested secondary source, not the retailer listing; corroborating headlines were seen but not fetched, so they do not count as separate documents.

dispersion: Retail quotes range from PNY ~$11,360 and Newegg ~$12,099 to B&H $13,349+, with refurbished at $9,500-$11,000.
